fixes.explanation: Yes, Israel. The man says, “Your name will no longer be Jacob, but Israel…” (Genesis 32:28). Later the Bible calls God's people "the Israelites," and the text here uses that word too (Genesis 32:32). I think Jacob walked in with one name and walked out with a brand new one.

Abraham is a good guess, since he was Jacob's grandfather. Abraham's son Isaac was Jacob's father (Genesis 25:19, 26). But the man gives Jacob a different name, “Israel” (Genesis 32:28). Abraham's name stays with Abraham.

Joshua doesn't come up in this passage at all. The man says, “Your name will no longer be Jacob, but Israel…” (Genesis 32:28). That's the name Jacob walks away with. Joshua can keep waiting in the wings, like me in that drawer, just with fewer dead batteries.

Thanks would be polite after a wrestling match that lasted until daybreak (Genesis 32:24). But the text doesn't say that. It says, “Then he blessed Jacob there.” (Genesis 32:29). A blessing is what Jacob asked for (Genesis 32:26).

Esau isn't Jacob's reason. Esau is Jacob's brother, and the passage gives no word of him here. Jacob's reason for the name is, “Indeed, I have seen God face to face, and yet my life was spared.” (Genesis 32:30). He names the place for what he saw.

That's the reason the text gives. “…the Israelites do not eat the tendon attached to the socket of the hip, because the socket of Jacob’s hip was struck near that tendon.” (Genesis 32:32). The text says "to this day," so it was still true when this was written.
The text never says anything about priests here. Its reason is, “…because the socket of Jacob’s hip was struck near that tendon.” (Genesis 32:32). The habit goes back to Jacob's hip.

Bowstrings are a creative guess, but the text doesn't mention them. It says the Israelites do not eat that tendon “…because the socket of Jacob’s hip was struck near that tendon.” (Genesis 32:32). The reason it gives goes back to Jacob's hip and that night at the Jabbok.
